plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Pale lavender-pink goblets rise straight from bare ground on leafless stems. The glossy leaves of spring are long gone, so the flowers seem to appear from nowhere. Clusters of them dot damp meadows and woodland edges as summer ends.
plants.bloomingSeason: August to September, so it is in flower on September 10
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges across Europe, and in cool-climate gardens in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Despite the name, it is not a true crocus or the source of saffron. All parts of the plant are highly toxic. It also yields colchicine, a compound that has been used in medicine and in plant breeding.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Australia's national floral emblem is covered in fluffy, fragrant golden pom-poms. Whole hillsides glow yellow against the grey-green foliage as winter turns to spring, and the blossoms draw in honeyeaters and bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (typically August and September), so it is in flower on September 10
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales, in woodlands and open forests
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates Wattle Day on September 1, the traditional start of spring, because the tree is in full bloom at that time.

plants.name: Hylotelephium spectabile
plants.description: Flat-topped flower heads, packed with tiny star-shaped blooms, open green and slowly deepen to rosy carmine. Thick, succulent grey-green leaves set them off. In early autumn the heads are alive with bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: August to September, so it is in flower on September 10
plants.location: Native to East Asia (China and Korea). Widely grown in temperate gardens in Europe and North America.
plants.funFact: The plant was long sold as Sedum spectabile, and many gardeners still know it by that name. Its fleshy leaves store water, which makes it tough in dry spells and a dependable late-season nectar source for pollinators.
